headline: Cocktail bomb explodes near PM's office in Tejgaon late Friday night; no casualties reported
summary: Miscreants detonated a cocktail bomb near the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon late Friday night. Police later recovered and defused an unexploded bomb from the scene, with no casualties reported.
details: Miscreants detonated a cocktail bomb near the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon late Friday night, around 1:15 AM on Friday, October 9. The incident involved two individuals on a motorcycle who quickly fled the scene after the explosion.
Police confirmed that there were no casualties or injuries from the blast. Authorities quickly secured the area and recovered an additional unexploded cocktail bomb from the site.

The unexploded device was safely defused by the police bomb disposal unit around 2:30 AM. Law enforcement agencies are actively working to identify and apprehend the two suspects involved in the incident.

Following the explosion, enhanced security measures have been implemented around the Prime Minister's Office. Traffic movement in the vicinity has also been controlled as part of the heightened security protocols.

headline: bKash manager shot, Tk 2.5 crore looted in Sreepur ambush
summary: A bKash cash manager was shot in the abdomen and three other employees were beaten during a robbery in Sreepur, Gazipur. Robbers made off with an estimated Tk 2.5 crore after ambushing their private car.
details: A bKash cash manager was shot and three other employees were severely beaten during a robbery in Sreepur, Gazipur. The incident occurred on Friday evening around 6:30 PM in the Karnapur area of the Sreepur-Gosinga regional road.

The robbers made off with an estimated Tk 2.5 crore, which was being transported in two sacks inside a private car. The funds had been collected from various bKash agents in Narsingdi and were en route to Maona.
The victim, Himel (35), an accounts manager for Valuka Channel Enterprise, was shot in the abdomen. The other injured employees were Md Fahad Hossain (30), Rifath (20), and driver Lal Mia (25).

According to the bKash employees, 15 to 20 unidentified assailants on motorcycles intercepted their car in a secluded, forested area. They shattered the car's windows, shot Himel, and dragged him out.
The other officials and the driver were mercilessly beaten. The robbers then seized two sacks filled with money from the car's trunk before fleeing the scene.

Following the attack, locals assisted the injured in reaching the Upazila Health Complex. Dr. Anik Sarkar of the emergency department confirmed Himel was transferred to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital due to his gunshot wound.
The other three received primary treatment at the Upazila Health Complex.

Sreepur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Shahinur Alam stated that bKash had not informed the police or 999 about transporting such a large sum of money. No police security was requested for the transfer.
Police were dispatched to the scene upon receiving the report. An investigation is underway, and legal action is being taken.
